sections.content:
149,520 people

were counted on the census as "waiters and waitresses" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Waiters and waitresses serve food and beverages in hotels, clubs, restaurants public houses and other establishments.

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "waiters and waitresses" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 16 to 19 years. Of the whole working population 2.4% were aged 16 to 19 years. For people working as "waiters and waitresses", 25.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "waiters and waitresses" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "waiters and waitresses" included:

  • bar staff
  • sports and leisure assistants
  • coffee shop workers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "waiters and waitresses" there were more women than men (71.1% compared with 28.9%).

This means "waiters and waitresses" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 28.9% and women made up 71.1% of "waiters and waitresses"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "waiters and waitresses" included:

  • local government administrative occupations
  • officers of non-governmental organisations
  • financial administrative occupations (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "waiters and waitresses" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "waiters and waitresses" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "waiters and waitresses", 8.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (75.3% compared with 24.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98%) than self-employed (2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
